1:1.headline: 'He is Ahasuerus': why the verse says his name twice
1:1.body: Rashi says the extra 'he is' means he stayed just as wicked from start to end. Ibn Ezra thinks it may set him apart from an earlier Persian king with the same name.

sources.quote: הוּא בְרִשְׁעוֹ מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ וְעַד סוֹפוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says he was the same in his wickedness from beginning to end.

sources.quote: ויתכן שהיה במלכי פרס הקדמונים מלך ששמו אחשורוש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says there may have been an earlier Persian king also named Ahasuerus.

1:1.headline: 'The one who reigned': a king who made himself king
1:1.body: The verse calls him המלך, 'the one reigning', and not simply 'the king'. Rashi says he took the throne on his own and was not born into the royal family.

sources.quote: שֶׁמָּלַךְ מֵעַצְמוֹ וְלֹא הָיָה מִזֶּרַע הַמְּלוּכָה
sources.says: Rashi says he became king by himself and was not of royal blood.

sources.quote: מספר כי אחשורוש לא היה מזרע המלוכה
sources.says: Malbim also reads the verse as telling us Ahasuerus was not of the royal line.

1:1.headline: India and Kush: two ends of the earth, or next door?
1:1.body: From Hodu (India) to Kush sounds like a huge span. Rashi says the two lands lay side by side, and he ruled all 127 provinces the way he ruled those two neighbors.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּלַךְ מֵהֹדוּ וְעַד כּוּשׁ שֶׁעוֹמְדִים זֶה אֵצֶל זֶה
sources.says: Rashi says he ruled 127 provinces just as he ruled from Hodu to Kush, which stand next to each other.

1:2.headline: 'When the king sat': firm on the throne, or resting from war
1:2.body: Rashi reads 'sat' as the moment his rule became firm in his hands. Ibn Ezra reads it as rest: he had stopped fighting the wars of Hodu and Kush.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁנִּתְקַיֵּם הַמַּלְכוּת בְּיָדוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means when the kingdom became established in his hand.

sources.quote: וטעם כשבת המלך אחשורוש ששקט ממלחמות הודו וכוש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means he was at rest from the wars of Hodu and Kush.

1:6.headline: Chur means white, the same root as Judah's nobles
1:6.body: Ralbag and Ibn Ezra say חור is white cloth. Ibn Ezra links it to חורי יהודה, the nobles of Judah, and says Aramaic uses the word the same way.

sources.quote: חור. עין והוא לבן מגזרת חורי יהודה וככה בלשון ארמית
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says chur is a color, white, from the same root as 'the nobles of Judah', and so in Aramaic.

sources.quote: חור הוא בגד לבן
sources.says: Ralbag says chur is a white cloth.

1:8.headline: No one forced the guests to drink
1:8.body: Rashi says some feasts made guests drain a large cup, but here no one was forced. Ibn Ezra explains אנס as forcing and ties it to the Aramaic phrase כל רז לא אנס לך, 'no secret is too hard for you'.

sources.quote: שֶׁכּוֹפִין אֶת הַמְּסֻבִּין לִשְׁתּוֹת כְּלִי גָדוֹל
sources.says: Rashi says some feasts force the guests to drink a large vessel, but not this one.

sources.quote: אונס. מכריח וקרוב מטעם וכל רז לא אנס לך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word means forcing, close in sense to the Aramaic 'no secret is hard for you'.

1:12.headline: Why did Vashti refuse? A hidden reason and a plain one
1:12.body: Rashi brings the sages: a skin disease broke out on her so she would refuse and be killed. Ralbag gives a plain reason: in her pride she wanted nobles, not servants, sent to fetch her.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁפָּרְחָה בָהּ צָרַעַת כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּמָאֵן וְתֵהָרֵג
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages that a skin disease broke out on her so that she would refuse and be killed.

sources.quote: כי לגאותה היתה רוצה שישלח לה אחשורוש שרים רבים נכבדים מאלה
sources.says: Ralbag says that out of pride she wanted the king to send more honored officials than these.

1:13.headline: 'Those who know the times': stargazers, historians, or judges?
1:13.body: Ibn Ezra and Ralbag say they read the stars, and Ibn Ezra also allows that they knew what happened to earlier kings. Malbim says they were judges who weighed the time and setting of an offense against the king.

sources.quote: חכמי המזלות או העתים שעברו על המלכים הקדמונים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they were experts in the stars, or in the times that passed over earlier kings.

sources.quote: שהיו בקיאים בחכמת המזלות
sources.says: Ralbag says they were skilled in the study of the stars.

sources.quote: היו צריכים לדעת את העתים, לדון לפי השעה והזמן
sources.says: Malbim says these judges had to know the times, to judge by the hour and the setting.

1:19.headline: 'Better than her', or 'better because of her'?
1:19.body: Plainly, the queen's place goes to a woman better than Vashti. Malbim reads the מ as 'because of': the next queen will behave better because she learned from Vashti's fate.

sources.quote: המ"ם הוא מ' הסבה שעל ידה תוסר ותהיה טובה
sources.says: Malbim says the letter mem here means 'because of': through Vashti the next queen will take the lesson and be good.

sources.quote: כי השנית תלמד מוסר מן ושתי
sources.says: Malbim says the second queen will learn a lesson from Vashti.

2:3.headline: Beauty treatments named from a word for scouring
2:3.body: Rashi ties תמרוקים to the scouring and rinsing of a pot. He says they are pleasant oils and spices that cleanse and soften the skin.

sources.quote: הֵן דְּבָרִים הַמְצַחְצְחִין כְּמוֹ "וּמֹרַק וְשֻׁטַּף."
sources.says: Rashi says they are polishing things, from the same word as scoured and rinsed.

sources.quote: שֶׁמֶן עָרֵב וּמִינֵי סַמָּנִים וּבְשָׂמִים הַמְטַהֲרִין וּמְעַדְּנִין אֶת הַבָּשָׂר
sources.says: Rashi says they are pleasant oil, herbs and spices that cleanse and soften the skin.

sources.quote: תמרקיהן. כמו תמרוק ברע
sources.says: Ibn Ezra compares the word to תמרוק in Proverbs.

2:5.headline: A Benjaminite called a Judean
2:5.body: Mordechai was from the tribe of Benjamin, yet he is called יהודי, a Judean. Rashi says everyone exiled with the kings of Judah was called a Judean among the nations, even those from another tribe.

sources.quote: עַל שֶׁגָּלָה עִם גָּלוּת יְהוּדָה. כָּל אוֹתָן שֶׁגָּלוּ עִם מַלְכֵי יְהוּדָה הָיוּ קְרוּיִים
sources.says: Rashi says he is called a Judean because he was exiled with the exile of Judah, and all those exiles were called Judeans.

sources.quote: איש יהודי. בעבור היותו ממלכות יהודה נקרא כן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he is called this because he was from the kingdom of Judah.

sources.quote: אִישׁ יְמִינִי. מִבִּנְיָמִין הָיָה, כַּךְ פְּשׁוּטוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the plain meaning of איש ימיני is that he was from Benjamin.

2:5.headline: Is this Kish the father of King Saul?
2:5.body: Rashi and Malbim treat Mordechai and Esther as members of King Saul's family. Ibn Ezra doubts it: if this Kish were Saul's father, the verse would have named Saul, the king, so we cannot know.

sources.quote: ואילו היה אבי שאול היה מזכיר שאול כי הוא מלך ולא אביו על כן לא נודע אם מרדכי הוא מבני שאול אם לא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says if Kish were Saul's father the verse would mention Saul, so it is unknown whether Mordechai descends from Saul.

sources.quote: שֶׁאִם יֵדְעוּ שֶׁהִיא מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת שָׁאוּל הַמֶּלֶךְ הָיוּ מַחֲזִיקִים בָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says Esther was from the family of King Saul.

sources.quote: ובשגם שהיה מזרע המלוכה מבני שאול
sources.says: Malbim says Mordechai was of royal descent, from Saul's line.

2:7.headline: Hadassah, the myrtle: a name for her good character
2:7.body: הדסה means myrtle, and Ralbag says she earned the name because, as a myrtle gives off a sweet smell, her good character did good to everyone near her. Ibn Ezra cites a midrash that drew a greenish skin tone from the name.

sources.quote: כי כמו שההדס יתן ריחו הטוב ויועיל בזה למי שאצלו כן היא נותנת ריחה בטוב מדותיה
sources.says: Ralbag says as the myrtle gives its good smell to those near it, so she gave hers through her good qualities.

sources.quote: ואפשר עוד שהיו לה שתי שמות
sources.says: Ralbag also allows that she simply had two names.

sources.quote: ודרש ירקרוקת מטעם הדסה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra mentions the midrash that she was greenish, drawn from the name Hadassah.

2:7.headline: As a daughter, or as a wife? One letter apart
2:7.body: The verse says Mordechai took Esther as a daughter, לבת. Rashi brings the Sages, who read it as לבית, for a household, meaning as a wife, and Ibn Ezra suggests the midrash arose because he had meant to marry her.

sources.quote: לוֹ לְבַת. רַבּוֹתֵינוּ פֵּרְשׁוּ "לְבַיִת", לְאִשָּׁה
sources.says: Rashi says the Sages read לבת as לבית, meaning as a wife.

sources.quote: אולי דרש לבית שהיה במחשבתו בעבור יופי' לקחתה לאשה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra suggests the reading לבית comes from Mordechai having planned to marry her for her beauty.

2:11.headline: What would become of her: Mordechai sensed a rescue coming
2:11.body: Rashi says Mordechai reasoned that such a righteous woman was taken only so she could one day save Israel, so he checked daily to see how it would end. Malbim says he feared she would be punished or sent away.

sources.quote: לֹא אֵרַע לְצַדֶּקֶת זוּ שֶׁתִּלָּקַח לְמִשְׁכַּב נָכְרִי אֶלָּא שֶׁעֲתִידָה לָקוּם לְהוֹשִׁיעַ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says Mordechai reasoned she was taken only because she would rise to save Israel.

sources.quote: ר"ל אם יענישוה או יגרשוה
sources.says: Malbim says Mordechai wanted to know whether they would punish her or send her away.

2:12.headline: A girl's turn, like the turtledove that comes on time
2:12.body: תר means a turn or a set time. Ibn Ezra notes that some tie it to the תור, the turtledove, which arrives at a fixed season.

sources.quote: תר נערה. כמו עת ויש אומרים מגזרת תור כי הוא יבא לעת מזומנת כטעם וקול התור
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says תר is like עת, a time, and some derive it from the turtledove, which comes at a set time.

2:14.headline: A second house, or returning a second time?
2:14.body: Rashi and Ralbag read שני as a second women's house, the one for the concubines. Ibn Ezra reads it as a second time: she went back to the women's house once more.

sources.quote: אֶל בֵּית הַנָּשִׁים שֵׁנִי. הַשֵּׁנִי
sources.says: Rashi says it means the second house of women.

sources.quote: הנה היה שם בית הנשים שני יבואו בו הפילגשים
sources.says: Ralbag says there was a second women's house where the concubines went.

sources.quote: הטעם פעם שני ובא הטעם לשון זכר כמו אך בפעם הזה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means a second time, in the masculine form as in בפעם הזה.

2:15.headline: Esther asked for nothing: good sense, or quiet refusal?
2:15.body: Every other girl could take whatever she asked for. Ibn Ezra says Esther's asking for nothing shows her good sense, while Malbim says it showed she was taken by force and did not come willingly.

sources.quote: לא בקשה דבר גם זה לאות על שכלה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says asking for nothing was a sign of her intelligence.

sources.quote: כי הראית בפועל שהיא אנוסה ואינה מתרצית אליו
sources.says: Malbim says she showed by her actions that she was forced and did not consent to him.

2:16.headline: Tevet: a Babylonian name for the tenth month
2:16.body: Ibn Ezra notes that Tevet is the Chaldean name, while Hebrew counted the months by number from the spring. Rashi adds that the tenth month is the cold season, when bodies warm each other, and God timed it to make her dear to the king.

sources.quote: כן יקרא בלשון כשדים ונקראו החדשים בלשון הקדש על המספר בעבור האביב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Tevet is the Chaldean name, and in Hebrew the months were numbered from the spring.

sources.quote: עֵת צִנָּה שֶׁהַגּוּף נֶהֱנֶה מִן הַגּוּף
sources.says: Rashi says the tenth month is the cold season, when one body enjoys the warmth of another, and God arranged it to endear her to the king.

2:17.headline: More than all the women, and more than all the maidens
2:17.body: The verse sets women beside maidens. Rashi says the king had gathered married women too, and Malbim says the women were his earlier wives and concubines, for whom the word love fits, while for the maidens the word is favor.

sources.quote: הַבְּעוּלוֹת, שֶׁאַף נָשִׁים הַבְּעוּלוֹת קִבֵּץ
sources.says: Rashi says the women were married women, since he gathered them too.

sources.quote: באין ספק היו לאחשורוש נשים ופילגשים גם מכבר, ואצלם שייך אהבה
sources.says: Malbim says Ahasuerus already had wives and concubines, and love is the word used for them.

2:18.headline: A one-time word: tax relief, or a day off?
2:18.body: הנחה, a release, appears only here. Rashi reads it as a tax break in Esther's honor, meant to coax her into revealing her birthplace, and Ralbag reads it as a day of rest from work on the wedding day.

sources.quote: לִכְבוֹדָהּ הֵנִיחַ לָהֶם מִן הַמַּס שֶׁעֲלֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says in her honor the king relieved the provinces of their tax.

sources.quote: וְהַכֹּל כְּדֵי לְפַתּוֹתָהּ אוּלַי תַּגִּיד מוֹלַדְתָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says it was all to coax her into revealing her birthplace.

sources.quote: רוצה לומר שצוה למדינות שינוחו ממלאכה ביום שנשא אסתר לאשה
sources.says: Ralbag says the king ordered the provinces to rest from work on the day he married Esther.

sources.quote: והנחה שם כמו מנוחה בעבור שמחתו באסתר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says הנחה is a noun like מנוחה, rest, given for his joy in Esther.

2:19.headline: Why gather maidens again after crowning Esther?
2:19.body: Ralbag says the king gathered them to check whether any was lovelier than Esther. Malbim says he gathered the rest and sent them home, so Esther could feel sure no one would replace her.

sources.quote: לעיין אם יש יותר יפה ממנה בבתולות
sources.says: Ralbag says the second gathering was to see whether any maiden was more beautiful than Esther.

sources.quote: הנה כבר קבץ את הבתולות הנשארות שעדיין לא נבעלו ושלחם לביתן
sources.says: Malbim says the king gathered the remaining maidens and sent them home.

2:22.headline: How did Mordechai learn of the plot?
2:22.body: The verse only says it became known to him. Rashi says the two plotters talked in their own language, not knowing Mordechai knew seventy languages, while Ralbag also allows holy inspiration or their gestures, and Ibn Ezra notes the text does not say.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיוּ מְסַפְּרִים דִּבְרֵיהֶם לְפָנָיו בְּלָשׁוֹן טוּרְסִי, וְאֵין יוֹדְעִים שֶׁהָיָה מָרְדְּכַי מַכִּיר בְּשִׁבְעִים לְשׁוֹנוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says they spoke in front of him in the Tarsian language, not knowing Mordechai knew seventy languages.

sources.quote: או נודע לו זה ברוח הקדש. או מצד רמיזותיהם
sources.says: Ralbag says he may also have learned it by holy inspiration or from their hints.

sources.quote: והכתוב לא הזכיר למה קצפו ואיך ידע הדבר מרדכי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra notes that the verse does not say why they were angry or how Mordechai found out.

3:2.headline: Bowing as honor, or bowing as worship
3:2.body: People bowed to high officials all the time. Rashi says Haman had made himself a god, so bowing to him meant worship. Malbim draws the line: bowing to Haman from afar was worship, but bowing in front of him was only respect for his rank.

sources.quote: שֶׁעָשָׂה עַצְמוֹ אֱלוֹהַּ, לְפִיכָךְ, וּמָרְדְּכַי לֹא יִכְרַע וְלֹא יִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה
sources.says: Rashi says Haman made himself a god, and that is why Mordecai would not kneel or bow.

sources.quote: כי צורת צלם וע"ז היו בבגדיו או על מצנפתו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites the Sages that an idol's image was on Haman's clothes or his headdress.

sources.quote: שלא ישתחוה לו בעת שהמן הולך מרחוק ואינו רואה, שאז אינו משתחוה רק מצד שעשה עצמו אלוה
sources.says: Malbim says bowing when Haman was far off and could not see would only be because he had made himself a god.

sources.quote: אבל אם משתחוה לו בעת שהמן רואה אותו, שאז אין זה לשם אלהות רק מצד שררותו
sources.says: He says bowing while Haman saw him would not be worship, only respect for his office.

4:1.headline: How did Mordecai know? A dream, or God's guiding hand
4:1.body: The full plan was secret, so how did Mordecai know everything that was done? Rashi says a dream told him heaven had agreed to the decree, and Malbim says God's providence let him learn even the secret dealings.

sources.quote: בַּעַל הַחֲלוֹם אָמַר לוֹ שֶׁהִסְכִּימוּ הָעֶלְיוֹנִים עַל כָּךְ
sources.says: Rashi says the 'master of dreams' told him that heaven had agreed to it.

sources.quote: נודע הדבר למרדכי ע"י השגחת ה' וידע כל הדברים שעברו בינו ובין המלך
sources.says: Malbim says Mordecai learned it through God's providence, including everything that passed between Haman and the king.

4:5.headline: Was Hatach really Daniel? Ibn Ezra doubts it
4:5.body: One lone opinion says Esther's messenger Hatach was Daniel. Ibn Ezra thinks it unlikely, because Daniel did not live into the reign of Ahasuerus.

sources.quote: יש בדברי יחיד שהתך הוא דניאל והקרוב אלי כי לא נמשכו ימיו עד מלוך אחשורוש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports a single opinion that Hatach is Daniel, but thinks Daniel did not live until Ahasuerus reigned.

4:14.headline: 'For a time like this': a purpose, or a warning?
4:14.body: Ibn Ezra and Ralbag read it as purpose: perhaps you became queen just to save Israel now. Rashi reads it as a warning: who knows if the king will still want you next year, when the killing is set.

sources.quote: מי יודע שמא לא הגעת למלכות אלא בעבור העת הזאת שתושיעי את ישראל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says perhaps she became queen only for this moment, to save Israel.

sources.quote: ומי יודע אם בעבור עת כזאת שהוא עת רעה לישראל הגעת למלכות
sources.says: Ralbag says perhaps she reached the throne for this bad time, so that rescue would come through her.

sources.quote: וּמִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם יַחְפֹּץ בָּךְ הַמֶּלֶךְ לַשָּׁנָה הַבָּאָה שֶׁהוּא זְמַן הַהֲרֵגָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means: who knows if the king will still want you next year, at the time set for the killing.

4:16.headline: 'If I perish, I perish': lost to death, or lost to Mordecai?
4:16.body: Plainly, Esther accepts she may die. A midrash Rashi brings hears more: as she was lost to her father's house, she will now be lost to Mordecai too.

sources.quote: וְכַאֲשֶׁר הִתְחַלְתִּי לֵילֵךְ לְאִבּוּד אֵלֵךְ וְאָמוּת
sources.says: Rashi says it means: as I have begun going toward ruin, I will go and die.

sources.quote: כַּאֲשֶׁר אָבַדְתִּי מִבֵּית אַבָּא אֹבַד מִמֶּךָ
sources.says: Rashi brings a midrash: as I was lost from my father's house, I will be lost from you.

sources.quote: ובא פועל עבר תחת עתיד, והטעם על מחשבתה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says a past-tense verb stands for the future here, describing what she expects.

4:17.headline: Mordecai 'passed through' the city, or 'passed over' the law?
4:17.body: ויעבר can mean 'he went across' or 'he broke a rule'. Malbim and Ralbag say he went through the streets, while Rashi says he broke the law by fasting on the first day of Passover.

sources.quote: עַל דָּת, לְהִתְעַנּוֹת בְּיוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח
sources.says: Rashi says he went against the law by fasting on the first festival day of Passover.

sources.quote: ויעבור בכל רחובות היהודים וגזר תענית
sources.says: Malbim says he went through all the Jewish streets and declared a fast.

sources.quote: שכבר עבר מרדכי בעיר שושן לכנוס את כל היהודים
sources.says: Ralbag says Mordecai went through the city of Shushan to gather all the Jews.

5:1.headline: She put on 'royalty': royal robes, or the holy spirit?
5:1.body: The verse says Esther put on מלכות, 'royalty', with no word for clothes. Rashi says it means royal robes, but the sages say she was clothed in the holy spirit, and Malbim says she wore kingship so naturally that everyone saw it suited her.

sources.quote: מַלְכוּת. בִּגְדֵי מַלְכוּת. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ: שֶׁלְּבָשַׁתָּה רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says it means royal clothes, and cites the sages: she was clothed in the holy spirit.

sources.quote: ותלבש אסתר מלכות. הטעם לבוש מלכות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the meaning is royal clothing.

sources.quote: המלכות לבשתה ויהי כמדה, עד שכל רואיה הכירו כי לה יאות המלוכה
sources.says: Malbim says kingship fit her like a garment, so all who saw her knew royalty suited her.

5:3.headline: 'Up to half the kingdom' may point to the Temple
5:3.body: By the plain sense the king offers up to half his empire. Rashi also gives the sages' reading: 'half' points to the thing in the middle of the kingdom, the Temple, whose building the kings had stopped.

sources.quote: דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא בְאֶמְצַע וּבַחֲצִי הַמַּלְכוּת. הוּא בֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says it means the thing in the middle of the kingdom, the Temple, whose building Cyrus and then Ahasuerus stopped.

sources.quote: וּפְשׁוּטוֹ שֶׁל מִקְרָא: אַף אִם תִּשְׁאֲלִי מִמֶּנִּי חֲצִי הַמַּלְכוּת, אֶתֵּן לָךְ
sources.says: Rashi says the plain sense is: even if you ask for half the kingdom, I will give it to you.

5:6.headline: A request and a plea: why the king asks for both
5:6.body: The king asks for Esther's שאלה and her בקשה. Malbim says others take the first as what is asked and the second as its purpose, but he holds that a שאלה is a small thing granted easily and a בקשה is a big thing that must be begged for.

sources.quote: המפרשים הבדילו בין שאלה ובקשה, כי בכל מבוקש מה שישאל תקרא שאלה, והתכלית הנרצה אל השואל תקרא בקשה
sources.says: Malbim says the commentators distinguish: the thing asked for is the שאלה, and the goal behind it is the בקשה.

sources.quote: שאלה הקטנה אשר ישיגה השואל בקל תקרא שאלה, והדבר הגדול שצריך לבקשו
sources.says: Malbim's own view: a small thing gotten easily is a שאלה, and a big thing that needs pleading is a בקשה.

5:9.headline: Mordecai did not even tremble before Haman
5:9.body: זע means to move, and also to shake with fear, the root of זועה, terror. Ibn Ezra and Malbim read it that way: Mordecai not only stayed seated, he showed no fear at all.

sources.quote: והנכון בעיני שהוא מן השניים כמו ביום שיזועו כטעם פחד ותנועה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word is like 'on the day they tremble', meaning fear and movement.

sources.quote: ראה שחוץ מה שלא קם מלפניו, אין לו שום יראה ופחד
sources.says: Malbim says Haman saw that besides not rising, Mordecai had no fear of him at all.

sources.quote: לְזַעֲוָה. מִגִּזְרַת ״לֹא קָם וְלֹא זָע״
sources.says: Rashi says זעוה, terror, comes from the same root as 'he did not rise or stir'.

5:11.headline: Many sons, or important sons? Why tell his own wife?
5:11.body: The grammarians read רב בניו as 'the greatness of his sons', since a man need not tell his wife how many sons he has. Ibn Ezra answers that Haman was boasting to his friends with his wife present, so it does mean many sons.

sources.quote: אמרו המדקדקים כי פירושו גדולת בניו כמו קרית מלך רב כי איך יגיד לאשתו שיש לו בנים רבים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports the grammarians: it means the greatness of his sons, because why would he tell his wife he has many sons?

sources.quote: ולפי דעתי שכן הוא ספר לאוהביו עם אשתו מזלו הטוב ויש לו עושר רב ובנים רבים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra's own view: Haman told his friends, together with his wife, of his good fortune, great wealth and many sons.

7:5.headline: Why does the verse say 'he said' twice?
7:5.body: Rashi cites a midrash: until now the king spoke to Esther through a messenger, but once he learned she was royal he spoke to her himself. Ibn Ezra says the repeat shows his sudden anger, and Ralbag says he first asked the people around him, then Esther.

sources.quote: בַּתְּחִלָּה הָיָה מְדַבֵּר עִמָּהּ עַל יְדֵי שָׁלִיחַ. עַכְשָׁיו שֶׁיָּדַע שֶׁמִּמִּשְׁפַּחַת מְלָכִים הִיא, דִּבֵּר עִמָּהּ הוּא בְעַצְמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says at first the king spoke with her through a messenger, and now that he knew she was from a royal family he spoke to her himself.

sources.quote: ויאמר פעמיים להורות שהמלך כעס מיד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'he said' appears twice to show the king became angry at once.

sources.quote: יתכן שאמר אחשורוש לאשר סביבו מי הוא זה ואי זה הוא
sources.says: Ralbag says the king may first have asked those around him who did this, and when no one answered he asked Esther.

7:6.headline: Adversary and enemy: Haman is both at once
7:6.body: Malbim says a צר harms someone in deed, while an אויב only wishes him harm. Most people stop hating once they have struck, but Haman's cruelty kept him an enemy even after he did harm.

sources.quote: כי צר הוא המציר לחברו בפועל ואויב המבקש רעת חבירו
sources.says: Malbim says a צר is one who actually harms another, and an אויב is one who wants harm for another.

sources.quote: אבל המן באכזריותו, הגם שהציר והרע עדיין הוא אויב
sources.says: Malbim says Haman in his cruelty stayed an enemy even after he had done harm.

7:6.headline: Haman was terrified because the king and queen sat together
7:6.body: נבעת means struck with terror. Malbim says Haman could have defended himself to the king alone, or begged the queen alone, but with both present any excuse to one would anger the other.

sources.quote: נבעת זורש והטעם כמו נבהל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says נבעת means the same as נבהל, terrified.

sources.quote: כי אל המלך עצמו היה יכול להתנצל להחזיק דבריו
sources.says: Malbim says Haman could have defended his words to the king alone.

sources.quote: נבעת מלפני המלך והמלכה בהיותם ביחד
sources.says: Malbim says he was terrified because the king and queen were together.

sources.quote: והמן נבעת. נחרד מצד המלך והמלכה
sources.says: Ralbag says Haman trembled because of both the king and the queen.

7:8.headline: Why was Haman falling on Esther's couch?
7:8.body: Rashi says an angel pushed him. Ibn Ezra says he was begging at her feet and fell from fear when the king came back, and Ralbag says he was bending over her couch to plead, which looked like an attack.

sources.quote: וְהָמָן נֹפֵל. הַמַּלְאָךְ דְּחָפוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says an angel pushed Haman.

sources.quote: שהיה מתחנן ומשתחוה לרגליה וכראותו כי שב המלך נפל מרוב פחדו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Haman was pleading and bowing at her feet, and when he saw the king return he fell from fear.

sources.quote: והיה כורע לדבר אליה במטה ההיא שהיא בו. ולזה היה דומה כאלו רצונו לכבוש אותה תחתיו
sources.says: Ralbag says Haman knelt on her couch to speak to her, so it looked as if he meant to force her.

7:8.headline: The word for conquering a land, used of forcing the queen
7:8.body: כבש is the verb for conquering a land. Rashi says the king means 'to force her by strength', as a land is subdued, and Ibn Ezra says it is a polite way of saying to lie with her by force.

sources.quote: הֲגַם לִכְבּוֹשׁ. לְשׁוֹן תֵּמַהּ הוּא. לִכְבּוֹשׁ לֶאֱנוֹס בְּחָזְקָה, כְּמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the king is exclaiming in shock, and לכבוש means to force by strength, as in 'the land was subdued'.

sources.quote: כינוי לשכיבה שתהיה מתחת רשותו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a polite term for lying with her against her will.

7:8.headline: They covered Haman's face, a Persian sign of the king's anger
7:8.body: חפו means they covered. Ibn Ezra says the king's servants covered the face of a man the king was angry with, so the king would not see him again.

sources.quote: כי כן משפט מלכי פרס שיכסו עבדי המלך פני מי שכעס עליו המלך שלא יראנו עוד המלך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it was the law of Persian kings that servants covered the face of one the king was angry with, so the king would not see him again.

sources.quote: אחשוב שכסו פניו שלא יראהו המלך לשכך חמת המלך
sources.says: Ralbag thinks they covered his face so the king would not see him, to calm the king's anger.

sources.quote: וחפו. ענין כסוי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means covering, citing this verse.

7:9.headline: Who was Harbonah: Elijah in disguise, or Haman's former ally?
7:9.body: Ibn Ezra reports that some say Harbonah was Elijah the prophet, appearing to the king as a palace servant. Rashi, citing the Talmud, says he had helped Haman and abandoned him when he fell.

sources.quote: יש אומרים כי אליה ז"ל נדמה למלך כדמות סריס
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports some who say Elijah appeared to the king in the form of a eunuch.

sources.quote: בֶּן עֲצָתוֹ שֶׁהָיָה מְסַיְּעוֹ בַּתְּחִלָּה, יִבְרַח מֵעֲזוֹר יָדוֹ בִּשְׁעַת כִּשְׁלוֹנוֹ. כְּמוֹ שֶׁעָשָׂה חַרְבוֹנָה לְהָמָן
sources.says: Rashi says the adviser who helped a man at first runs from him when he stumbles, as Harbonah did to Haman.

8:8.headline: 'Cannot be reversed': improper to undo, or forbidden by Persian law?
8:8.body: Rashi says אין להשיב means it is not fitting to undo the king's letter, because that would make it a forgery. Ibn Ezra says the king could not undo it, because that is the law of Media and Persia.

sources.quote: אֵין נָאֶה לַהֲשִׁיבוֹ וְלַעֲשׂוֹת כְּתַב הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּזִיּוּף
sources.says: Rashi says it is not fitting to undo it and make the king's letter a forgery.

sources.quote: לא אוכל להשיבם כי כן דת מדי ופרס
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the king told him he could not undo them, because that is the law of Media and Persia.

8:10.headline: אחשתרנים: swift camels, or mules?
8:10.body: Rashi says the word names a kind of camel that runs fast. Ibn Ezra says some explain it as mules.

sources.quote: הָאֲחַשְׁתְּרָנִים. מִין גְּמַלִּים הַמְמַהֲרִים לָרוּץ
sources.says: Rashi says אחשתרנים is a kind of camel that hurries to run.

sources.quote: האחשתרנים. י"א הפרדים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some say אחשתרנים are the mules.

8:10.headline: הרמכים, 'mares', is found in the language of Ishmael too
8:10.body: Ibn Ezra says הרמכים are mares, and says the same word is found in the language of Ishmael, whose words mostly follow the pattern of Hebrew. He adds that the foals of mares are stronger than those of donkeys.

sources.quote: הן הסוסיות וכן בלשון ישמעאל שרוב מתכונתה כדרך לשון הקדש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they are the mares, and so in the language of Ishmael, most of whose form follows the way of the holy language.

sources.quote: ובני הסוסיות חזקים מבני האתונות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the offspring of mares are stronger than those of she-donkeys.

8:15.headline: תכריך: a wrap, a cloak, or a headdress?
8:15.body: Rashi says תכריך is a wrap of fine linen, a garment to wrap oneself in. Ibn Ezra says it is like a cloak wound around the body. Ralbag thinks it was worn on the head.

sources.quote: מַעֲטֵה בּוּץ, טַלִּית הֶעָשׂוּי לְהִתְעַטֵּף
sources.says: Rashi says it is a covering of fine linen, a garment made for wrapping oneself.

sources.quote: והטעם כאדרת שיעולף בה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means like a cloak that one is wrapped in.

sources.quote: אחשוב שזה התכריך היה על ראשו
sources.says: Ralbag says he thinks this תכריך was on his head.

8:15.headline: 'The city of Shushan' rejoiced: only the Jews, or everyone?
8:15.body: Ibn Ezra says the city means the Jews who lived there. Ralbag gives that reading, and then says it is more correct that it means all the people of the city. Malbim agrees that all the nations rejoiced at Mordecai's rise.

sources.quote: והעיר שושן. ששם היהודים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'the city of Shushan' means the Jews who are there.

sources.quote: רוצה לומר היהודים אשר בשושן. או שב זה לכל אנשי העיר והוא היותר נכון
sources.says: Ralbag says it means the Jews in Shushan, or else all the people of the city, and that this is more correct.

sources.quote: שגם העמים כולם שמחו ברבות מרדכי הצדיק
sources.says: Malbim says that all the nations too rejoiced when the righteous Mordecai rose.

9:5.headline: An enemy hates in the open; a hater hides it
9:5.body: The verse uses two words, אויב 'enemy' and שונא 'hater'. Malbim says an enemy shows his hatred and a hater keeps it hidden. So the Jews killed only open enemies, and the hidden haters they could shame.

sources.quote: כי ההבדל בין אויב ושונא שהאויב איבתו גלויה, והשונא אין שנאתו גלויה
sources.says: Malbim says an enemy's hatred is open and a hater's is not.

sources.quote: רק ויעשו בשונאיהם כרצונם, שהיו יכולים לגנות אותם ולהשפילם
sources.says: Malbim says 'they did as they wished to their haters' means they could disgrace and humble them, not kill them.

9:13.headline: 'The tree' may be the same gallows Haman hung on
9:13.body: Esther asks that Haman's sons hang 'on the tree', not 'on a tree'. Ibn Ezra's second commentary says this means the known gallows where Haman was hanged, or one tall gallows for all ten.

sources.ref: Second Version of Ibn Ezra on Esther 9:13:2
sources.quote: על העץ הידוע שנתלה עליו המן או כולם נתלו על עץ אחד כי גבוה היה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'the tree' is the known tree Haman was hanged on, or one tree for all of them because it was tall.

9:22.headline: The poor are named for wanting
9:22.body: Ibn Ezra's second commentary takes אביון, a poor person, from the root אבה, 'to want'. The poor want everything, because they cannot afford it.

sources.ref: Second Version of Ibn Ezra on Esther 9:22:3
sources.quote: והמלה מגזרת אם תאבו כי הם מתאוים לכל דבר בעבור שאין ידם משגת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word comes from the root of 'if you are willing' (תאבו), because the poor long for everything they cannot reach.

9:26.headline: Purim is named after Haman's lot, the pur
9:26.body: The verse explains the name itself: the days are called Purim after the pur, the lot Haman cast. Malbim says the name recalls how Haman's lot was turned into a lot in the Jews' favor. Ibn Ezra's second commentary says the name is plural because the feast has two days.

sources.quote: שהשם פורים מורה עליו שפור המן נהפך לפורנו
sources.says: Malbim says the name Purim shows that Haman's lot was turned into our lot.

sources.ref: Second Version of Ibn Ezra on Esther 9:26:1
sources.quote: על כן וגו’ פורים. בעבור היותם שני ימים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the name is plural because there are two days.

9:26.headline: A letter is a gathering of words
9:26.body: Ibn Ezra ties אגרת, a letter, to the ant that 'gathers (אגרה) its food at harvest' in Proverbs. A letter, he says, is words gathered together.

sources.quote: מגזרת אגרה בקציר מאכלה והטעם מחברת המלים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra derives the word from 'gathers its food at harvest' and says it means a collection of words.

9:27.headline: 'Those who join them' are converts still to come
9:27.body: The Jews took on Purim for themselves, their children, and 'those who join them'. Rashi says these are people who will convert in the future. Ibn Ezra also reads it as converts, as in Isaiah's 'the foreigner who joins himself to the Lord'.

sources.quote: הַנִּלְוִים עֲלֵיהֶם. גֵּרִים הָעֲתִידִים לְהִתְגַּיֵּר
sources.says: Rashi says these are converts who will convert in the future.

sources.ref: Second Version of Ibn Ezra on Esther 9:27:2
sources.quote: והגרים הם הנלוים עליהם וכמו ואל יאמר בן הנכר הנלוה אל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they are converts, as in Isaiah's 'the foreigner who joins himself'.

9:27.headline: 'As written' becomes a rule about the scroll itself
9:27.body: ככתבם can simply mean 'as Mordecai wrote'. Rashi reads it as a rule that the scroll of Esther be written in the square Hebrew script. Ibn Ezra reads it as a hint that the scroll is to be read aloud.

sources.quote: כִּכְתָבָם. שֶׁתְּהֵא הַמְּגִלָּה כְתוּבָה כְּתָב אַשׁוּרִית
sources.says: Rashi says it means the scroll must be written in the square script (כתב אשורית).

sources.quote: ככתבם. הטעם שתקרא המגלה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means the scroll is to be read.

9:31.headline: Which fasts? Esther's fast, or the yearly fasts for Jerusalem
9:31.body: The verse does not say which fasts. Ibn Ezra's second commentary says it is not the three days Esther fasted, but the four yearly fasts for Jerusalem's fall. The people took those on by themselves, and in the same way took on Purim.

sources.ref: Second Version of Ibn Ezra on Esther 9:31:1
sources.quote: ואין טעם דברי הצומות על ג' ימים שהתענו רק הטעם על ד' הצומות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'the fasts' are not the three days they fasted but the four yearly fasts.

sources.quote: ממה שקימו וקבלו תחלה הארבעה צומות
sources.says: Malbim also says these are the four fasts the people had accepted before.

9:32.headline: 'Written in the book': this scroll, or a book now lost
9:32.body: Rashi says Esther asked the sages to place this book among the holy writings, and 'written in the book' means they did. Ibn Ezra says it was a book known in their day that has since been lost.

sources.quote: אֶסְתֵּר בִּקְשָׁה מֵאֵת חַכְמֵי הַדּוֹר לְקָבְעָהּ וְלִכְתֹּב סֵפֶר זֶה עִם שְׁאָר הַכְּתוּבִים
sources.says: Rashi says Esther asked the sages of her time to write this book among the other holy writings.

sources.quote: הוא הידוע בימיהם ואבד הספר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it was a book known in their days, and the book was lost.
